newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cancels U.S. horror film after Kobe killing.
newsitem.headline: Japan cancels U.S. horror film after Kobe killing.

text.p: Japanese distributors have indefinitely postponed the release of a blockbuster U.S. teen slasher film in the wake of the killing and beheading of an 11-year-old schoolboy, the company said on Monday.

"We have decided to postpone indefinitely the release of the film 'Scream' because the Kobe (murder) case remains unsolved and uncertainty is spreading throughout the country," Japan distributors Asmik Corp said in a statement.
"The theme and the story is unrelated to the Kobe case, but we found it inappropriate to run the movie now," Asmik said.

"Scream", released in the United States by Walt Disney Co's Miramax Films last year, is about a serial murder of students at a U.S. high school. The film was a box office hit in the United States and was scheduled to be released in Japan in mid-June.
The killing and beheading of schoolboy Jun Hase in the port town of Kobe in central Japan last month has sent shockwaves across the nation.

The boy left his home in a Kobe suburb shortly after noon on May 24, saying he was going to see his grandfather. Three days later his head was found at the foot of an iron gate of a nearby junior high school.
Inside the boy's mouth was a note which said the murderer enjoyed killing and planned to strike again.
Earlier this month, a person purporting to be the killer sent a letter to a local newspaper blaming Japan's draconian education system for the murderous urges he suffered.
